summary:
The bill, cited as the “Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2025,” appropriates funds for fiscal year ending September 30, 2025, for legislative branch entities and imposes related limitations and permanent-law amendments.

Title I appropriates, among other amounts, $174,000 to the widow of Representative Donald M. Payne, Jr.; $1,932,655,000 for House salaries and expenses, including leadership offices, Members’ Representational Allowances, intern compensation allowances, committee employees, House officers and employees, allowances and expenses, and $10,000,000 for the House Modernization Initiatives Account under 2 U.S.C. 5513, subject to House Appropriations approval and use only for initiatives approved by the Committee on House Administration. It appropriates funds for joint items, including the Joint Economic Committee, Joint Committee on Taxation, Office of the Attending Physician, and Office of Congressional Accessibility Services; $619,257,000 for Capitol Police salaries and $213,158,000 for general expenses, with overtime notification requirements and restrictions on certain China-manufactured drones except for national security purposes; and funds for the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights, Congressional Budget Office, Architect of the Capitol, Library of Congress, Government Publishing Office, Government Accountability Office, Congressional Office for International Leadership Fund, and John C. Stennis Center.

Administrative provisions in Title I require unobligated FY2025 Members’ Representational Allowance balances to be deposited for deficit reduction or debt reduction (sec. 110); cap vehicle lease payments from MRAs at $1,000 per month, excluding mobile district offices (sec. 111); require federal cybersecurity assistance to the House to preserve separation-of-powers integrity and minimize dissemination of privileged House and Member information (sec. 112); amend section 303(f) of the Energy Policy Act of 1992, 42 U.S.C. 13212(f), regarding long-term lease requirements, effective FY2025 and thereafter (sec. 113); and amend 2 U.S.C. 2062(d)(3) to authorize House Child Care Center revolving fund payment of specified telecommunications expenses (sec. 114). Section 115 amends 5 U.S.C. 4120 to require Capitol Police Board approval for Capitol Police training outside the United States. Section 117 authorizes, subject to appropriations-committee approval, Architect of the Capitol cooperative agreements supporting the Capitol Grounds and Arboretum and authorizes plant material exchanges. Section 118 caps FY2025 Library reimbursable and revolving fund obligational authority at $328,789,000.

Title II contains general limitations, including fiscal-year availability absent express provision (sec. 202), public-record requirements for consulting contracts under 5 U.S.C. 3109 (sec. 204), transfer restrictions (sec. 206), protections for Member-led Capitol tours subject to security restrictions (sec. 207), pornography-blocking requirements for funded networks with law-enforcement and official-activity exceptions (sec. 208), prohibitions on use of funds for covered telecommunications equipment or services with specified effective dates and a one-time waiver authority (sec. 209), pay-adjustment authority for the GPO Director and Librarian of Congress beginning calendar year 2025 (sec. 210), an amendment to 5 U.S.C. 13144 excluding Member medical or dental care relationships from fiduciary treatment for that section (sec. 211), restrictions on certain DEI training or implementation (sec. 212), restrictions on funding discriminatory actions based on specified marriage-related religious or moral beliefs (sec. 213), and a prohibition on FY2025 Member cost-of-living adjustments under 2 U.S.C. 4501 (sec. 214).
